historyIntro: Discover the places and milestones that shaped Cavinti, from its early parish to the present day.
historyChurchNarrative: The NHCP’s historical marker records that Cavinti’s ecclesiastical administration belonged to Lumbang until 1619. Its first stone church and convent were built around 1621.
historyUprisingNarrative: The early stone church and convent were severely damaged during the 1639 Chinese uprising, according to accounts of the parish church.
historyEarthquakeNarrative: The 1824 earthquake partly damaged the church and destroyed the convent. The present church was begun in 1834 and completed before 1851; a bell tower begun in 1822 was completed in 1831.
historyEarthquake1880Narrative: The 1880 earthquakes destroyed the church’s bell tower and damaged its walls, another interruption in the building’s long history.
historyCalirayaNarrative: Construction of Caliraya Dam began in 1939, creating a reservoir in the Cavinti area. A small hydroelectric plant began operating in 1942; the lake later became a setting for recreation as well as power generation.
historyPopulationNarrative: The Philippine Statistics Authority recorded 24,740 residents in Cavinti in the 2024 census. This is a census count, not a live population estimate.
historyDataNarrative: In June 2026, the Philippine Statistics Authority turned over Cavinti’s 2024 Community-Based Monitoring System data to the municipal government, providing local information for planning.
historyAct1240Narrative: On 5 October 1904, Act No. 1240 moved the seat of Luisiana’s municipal government to Cavinti and combined the two territories under Luisiana.
historyAct1712Narrative: On 12 September 1907, Act No. 1712 separated Cavinti from Luisiana and reconstituted it as a municipality, restoring its territory from before Act No. 939.
historyMarkerBody: The historical marker was unveiled in 1938 and installed by the Historical Research and Markers Committee.
historyWeavingBody: Cavinti’s Sambalilo Festival celebrates its pandan-weaving tradition and the local hats that give the festival its name.
historyFallsTitle: At the foot of the Sierra Madre
historyFallsBody: Cavinti is an upland Laguna municipality in the foothills of the Sierra Madre, bordering Quezon to the east.
historyCavesBody: The Cavinti Underground River and Caves Complex includes Cathedral Cave, whose entrance was discovered by DENR personnel in 2011.

accessibilityPolicy: The portal provides keyboard navigation, visible focus, labeled controls, semantic headings and language-preserving URLs. Record titles remain original when reviewed translations are unavailable. Report accessibility barriers through GitHub with the URL, browser and steps, without personal information.
privacyPolicy: The portal has no accounts, analytics, cookies or database. Language and filters are stored in URLs. The static host may retain access logs. When the map approaches the viewport, your browser requests styles, fonts and tiles from OpenFreeMap, which receives your IP address. Official portraits are loaded from the municipal website, which also receives your IP address. External sources and GitHub apply their own privacy policies; issues are public. Do not submit private phone numbers, patient or household details. Reports never update published data automatically.
